narrative:
The model predicts you have a 32% chance of failing your final year, which is high enough that the school requires you to take remedial courses to help strengthen your performance before it's too late.

The three factors that most influenced this decision were your lack of desire to pursue higher education, your reason for choosing this school, and your history of one past class failure. Your stated unwillingness to continue studying beyond high school was the strongest element pushing the prediction toward failure. Because every student who passed expressed a clear ambition for higher education, your response stood out as a major warning sign to the model.

Next, your choice of this school mainly because it was close to home worked in the opposite direction, mildly pulling the prediction toward passing. Most students who succeeded had chosen the school for its academic reputation or course offerings rather than convenience, so your reason gave the model some slight reassurance.

However, having already failed a class once was the third most important factor and pushed the outcome back toward failing. Students who passed had zero past failures on average, making your history a clear red flag.

To improve, you should seriously reflect on your goals. If you can reconnect with a reason to aim higher, protect your study time, and reduce absences (yours are more than double the average of those who passed), your chances can rise quickly. Remedial courses are there to help you rebuild these foundations.
